name: Null’s Apps
subtitle: NullSign and Lineup for iPhone and Apple TV
description: Unsigned iOS and tvOS app builds published after successful main-branch builds.

apps.name: NullSign
apps.subtitle: Sign and install iOS apps
apps.localizedDescription: A local iOS IPA signer and installer.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Full screen on iPhone Duo. The tab bar sits on the right like the rest of the phone, next to your toolbar buttons when it's tucked away.
• Switched to the regular iOS tab bar. Tap the tab you're already on to jump back to its first screen. The Signer badge still counts your waiting updates.
• Installs finish on Completed with a checkmark, even when iOS stops reporting progress right at the end.
• Deleting an app from your library happens right away, and you'll know if it didn't save. Imported apps show their real icons.
• If an IPA from Files won't import, you'll see why instead of it just disappearing.
• PPQ protection is gone. Apps are signed with their own bundle ID.
• A source with a missing file tells you that, instead of a confusing invalid JSON error. GitHub sources can drop out for a minute while a new release uploads.

• Fixed a crash when installing imported apps with ElleKit enabled.
• ElleKit is now enabled by default for new or reset signing settings. Your saved preference is kept.
• Invalid or incomplete .deb tweaks now show an error instead of closing NullSign.

• Tap Install on an imported app to sign it with your saved certificate and settings, then continue straight to installation.
• The same progress bar now follows preparation, signing, packaging and installation. Errors stay in the progress card with a Retry action.
• The usual iPhone install flow skips the browser's extra Open prompt while keeping iOS's Install confirmation. Continue in Browser is available if needed.
• Repository icons now update from the latest source feed when you refresh, including the icons beside All Apps.

• Fixed installs hanging in Safari and ending with "the server stopped responding" on some cellular carriers. NullSign now installs from your Wi-Fi address, never your cellular one.
• Without Wi-Fi, installs go through the phone itself, the same as the Use localhost only setting.

• New setting: Keep Only the Newest Version, in Settings › Signing Defaults › Library. When a newer version of an app arrives, older copies of it are deleted from Imported and from Signed.
• Turning it on clears out duplicate and older copies already in your library. Apps installed on your device stay installed.
• An older version you import on purpose is kept, and an app being signed or updated never loses the copy it just made.

• Update on a signed app now updates it in one tap. NullSign downloads the new version, signs it with the same certificate, then asks iOS to install it over the old one.
• While an app updates, its row shows Downloading update and Signing update, and if something goes wrong NullSign tells you why.
• Fixed tapping Update on a signed app reinstalling the version you already had.

• Apps you've already updated no longer say Update available. Once a newer copy is in your Library, the older copy stops offering the update and the Signer tab badge clears.
• Update badges refresh as soon as you add, sign or delete an app, without waiting for the next check.

• Improved compatibility with passwordless .p12 certificates.
• Certificate import now explains password problems, missing private keys and mismatched provisioning profiles.
• Improved reliability when importing several IPA or TIPA files together, including files with matching names.
• App names, versions and icons are preserved during import, and failed imports clean up partial files.

• You can update NullSign from inside the app. When a new version is out, the Signer tab shows a banner with an Update button. Tap it, then tap Install when iOS asks.
• The update is signed with the certificate on your Signer tab. The app drops to the Home Screen while iOS installs it, so open it again once the icon finishes.
• Check for Updates now looks for a new NullSign as well as your apps, and it has its own button, apart from the + button.
• Apps you imported from Files now get updates when one of your sources lists a newer version.
• This is the last version you'll have to download by hand.

• Check for Updates in your Library now says what it does, then tells you whether everything is up to date or how many updates it found.
• The Signer tab shows a red count when apps have updates, so you can see them from any tab.
• Coming back after a while checks again, so you hear about new builds even if the app stays open for days.

• Versions now show their build number in parentheses, like 0.19.0 (960), in your sources, version history and Library, so you can tell builds apart.
• A newer build of the same version now shows up as an update.
• Settings › About finds NullSign updates again.

• Fixed signing failures caused by unreadable files inside an imported app.
• Imported apps now stay clear of the bottom navigation bar.
• Refreshed the dark interface, with more consistent cards, menus and controls.
• Improved artwork when importing Apple TV apps.
• Removed repeated Apple TV installation prompts.

apps.name: Lineup
apps.subtitle: Live TV, sports, and your media library
apps.localizedDescription: Lineup puts your IPTV provider and your media servers in one app. Watch live channels with a full TV guide, catch up on what you missed, or put two channels side by side. Find any game in Sports and jump straight to the channel showing it. Browse movies and shows from Jellyfin, Emby, Plex or Silo, pick up where you left off, and request what's missing through Seerr. Inspired by Janky and Stadium-Sync.

versions.localizedDescription:
• The smaller iPhone download includes AetherEngine 7.62.1 and MPVKit. MPVKit can take over when AetherEngine can’t open a stream.
• The Library hero uses backdrop artwork. Pick multiple catalogs for the hero or shuffle titles across your catalogs.
• You can hide the built-in genre categories in Search and move stream badges above the server’s formatted text.
• Switching My Teams or changing leagues now starts the schedule at the top, with live games and upcoming days in separate rows.

• Continue Watching shows the series name and poster, with one thin bar along the bottom for the episode or movie you paused.
• Switch Jellyfin profiles from the Library and see each person's profile picture. You can also sign in with Quick Connect.
• On AIO Jellyfin servers, Continue Watching follows the selected profile's resume list.
• The TV Guide keeps the last channel in view when you scroll to the bottom or change categories.
• Look for Lineup's new three-bar icon on your Home Screen.

• Shows you're caught up on stay in Continue Watching, with the next episode's air date, or a Coming Soon card until one is scheduled.
• With two servers connected, like Nullfin and AIOStreams, a movie or show shows up once in Continue Watching, and your progress reaches both servers whichever one played it.
• Continue Watching keeps up with your other devices: something you finish on the Apple TV moves on here too, and Lineup checks again whenever you come back to the app.
• Nullfin and other Jellyfin servers' streams now show exactly the way your formatter writes them, like AIOStreams' do.
• Games that won't load move to another channel within about 15 seconds instead of minutes, and Lineup remembers channels that failed and tries the working ones first next time.
• Ambient Mode spreads the picture's colours into the black bars around it, like YouTube. Turn it off in Metadata settings.
• Show names in the TV Guide no longer carry the tiny raised "New" some providers add; new episodes get a clean NEW badge instead.

• The player has a new look built on Liquid Glass on iOS 26: close at the top left, picture in picture at the top right, bigger play and skip buttons in the middle, and the title right on the picture instead of in a box.
• Subtitles, audio, the next episode and the summary are together in one toolbar at the bottom right, and the progress bar is a thin line along the bottom.
• Full screen in Sports and the TV Guide, the player has the same look, with live stats and other channels for the game in the toolbar at the bottom right.

• Your progress now syncs with Jellyfin, Emby and AIOStreams. The server knows where you stopped, and what you watch in other apps shows up in Continue Watching and Next Up. You can turn it off with Server Tracking in your tracking settings.
• AIOStreams streams are listed exactly the way your formatter writes them. Turn off Server's Stream Format in Metadata settings to go back to Lineup's own layout.
• Add badge packs by link under Stream Badges, and streams get picture badges for things like 4K, Dolby Vision or Atmos. Packs made for the AIOStreams app, Fusion or Nuvio work as they are.
• AIOStreams streams come up faster: Lineup starts finding them as soon as you open a movie or episode.
• Posters from your own server, such as ones from a poster service, now stay put instead of being swapped for TMDB's. Server Posters in Metadata settings turns this off.
• Collection, folder and streaming service cards no longer leave empty space under their names.
• The player's buttons and panels use Liquid Glass on iOS 26.
• Late games that run past midnight stay on the Sports list until they end, wherever you are.

• Finishing the newest episode of a show that's still airing keeps your place. It no longer jumps to the specials or back to the first episode, and the next episode shows up in Continue Watching once it's announced.
• Episode cards show the air date and running time right under the episode's name.
• Adding an AIOStreams server sets up your Library straight away: its libraries appear as shelves in the order you arranged them, and the banner at the top fills itself.
• AIOStreams collections show their full wide artwork instead of being cropped, and the banner at the top of Library only features movies and shows, never collection art.
• You can now remove the Collections row from the Library's Remove Shelf menu, and bring it back from Add Shelf.
• Library lists no longer say "0 titles" for libraries whose size the server doesn't report.

• The posters in Library's Streaming Services row now come to life. Each one shows art from that service's most popular titles you can play, drifting slowly and fading to the next title every few seconds.
• The posters stay smooth while you scroll and take turns changing, so the row never changes all at once. With Reduce Motion on, each poster shows a still picture instead.
• With an AIOStreams server added, Library opens faster and stays lighter: Lineup no longer loads every one of your catalogs each time you open the app. Your collections still show in the Collections row, and a collection's titles load when you open it.
• When there's no featured banner at the top of Library, the first row no longer sits under the clock.

• Reduced slowdowns when opening live events, switching tabs and browsing large libraries while channels and guide data refresh in the background.
• Settings scrolls smoothly as the navigation bar compacts and reappears.
• Live scores refresh independently of channel matching, and tennis events keep their prepared channels when tournament listings change.
• Fixed an earlier stream starting after you had already stopped playback or selected another stream.
• Added soccer coverage for the Carabao Cup, FA Cup, Copa del Rey and Supercopa de España.
• Device Reports in Diagnostics can now copy saved reports with the installed build and iOS version.
• This iPhone release has no user-facing changes.

• Returning to Lineup shows saved live events and their matched channels sooner, so you can open a game while schedules and TV listings refresh in the background.
• Saved alternative channels are ready alongside the main feed, including when the original channel's listing has ended.
• The data refresh popup now appears only in TV Guide.
• The glass navigation bar compacts and expands with a smoother transition, respecting Reduce Motion.

• Playlist guides that wouldn't load now do. Lineup used to throw out a whole guide over one badly written listing, a very large guide or a slow guide server, which left the TV Guide empty and Sports with nothing to match.
• A listing Lineup can't read is now skipped on its own, so the rest of the guide still shows.
• If a provider's channels or guide still won't load, the TV Guide now says why.

• The AetherEngine player is updated to 7.49.0, and Settings shows the new version.
• Resuming a film or an episode no longer jumps to 0:00 for a moment as it starts, which could also save your place as the very beginning.
• Pressing Play after a pause no longer flashes the loading spinner.
• Some MP4 videos that stuttered or showed frames out of order now play smoothly, and MP4s with lots of subtitle tracks no longer keep stopping to buffer.
• Films with picture-based subtitles, such as those from Blu-rays, use far less memory.
• Disconnecting headphones, a Bluetooth speaker or AirPlay now pauses the video, as Apple's own player does.
• Includes a security fix for teletext captions on TV channels.

• Settings is now the same black as the rest of the app. The glow in your accent colour stays in the top corner, and the blue tint lower down is gone.
• The bar and title across the top of Settings are gone, so your settings start right under the clock.
• Pages you open from Settings still have their title and back button.

• Setting up an Apple TV now keeps each show where you're furthest along. If the TV is a few episodes ahead of your iPhone, it stays there, even if you played an earlier episode on your iPhone more recently.
• The same goes the other way: if your iPhone is further into a show, the TV moves on to where you are.
• Episodes and movies you've finished on either device still count as watched, and where both have played the same one, the further point wins.

• You can now set up an Apple TV from your iPhone. On the TV, choose Set Up with iPhone, then scan the code it shows with your camera or from Settings › Set Up Apple TV.
• Your IPTV providers, media servers and their sign-ins go across in one step, along with MDBList, Seerr, favorites, My Teams and your settings. It all travels over your Wi-Fi, locked with the code on the TV.
• Watch history comes too. Anything either device has watched is kept, and where both played the same title, the most recent play wins.
• A server or provider the TV already has is updated instead of being added a second time.

• Text across the app now uses Apple's own rounded system font instead of one bundled with Lineup, so the download is a little smaller.
• From now on, every build has its own number, so your signing app will always offer a new release as an update. That's why this one jumps from 155 to 943.

• Your watch history and favorites take up far less space. Resume points, watched marks and favorites are all kept, and a title's cast, trailers and other details still load from your server when you open it.
• Subtitles you download while watching no longer pile up on your phone after you close the app.
• If the last update didn't show up in your signing app, this one will. It has a new build number.

• Menus are now dark and see-through, like the welcome screen's sign-in card, so you can see what's behind them while every row stays easy to read. Settings has the same look.
• The league menu on the Sports tab shows each league as a card in its logo's colors.
• The Library shows Trending and the streaming-service rows before you connect a media server. Open one of those titles to see its details and a button for adding a server.
• In the TV Guide, adding, removing or moving a favorite no longer jumps the list back to the top, and each move in the reorder sheet is saved as soon as you make it.
• Seerr has moved out of the TV Guide menu. You'll still find it in the Library.
• Signing in to Silo now works like Jellyfin and Emby, with a choice between your account and an API key.
• The local network permission prompt now names Jellyfin, Emby, Plex and Silo.

• Use more than one IPTV provider at a time, with provider names shown alongside channels so you know where each feed comes from.
• Added Seerr for discovering and requesting titles, plus Silo as another way to connect your media library.
• Choose local tracking, MDBList, or both. Continue Watching also handles MDBList-only progress more reliably.
• Movie and show logos can appear as soon as one artwork source is ready, and previously loaded logos are reused when you return.
• Opening a title from Nullfin no longer starts an unnecessary stream lookup before showing its details.
• Search genres are now in A–Z order. Tapping Search again takes you back to the main genre screen.
• Refreshed Library pages, cast photos, sign-in screens and menus. Similar Movies and Shows now comes from TMDB.
• Added a Native player option with a clearly labeled AetherEngine fallback, ATP/WTA following, and more control over TV Guide categories.
• Lineup has a new red play icon, and the welcome screen now uses a subtle animated background.

• The TV Guide and Sports lists have a new look, with row colors drawn from each channel's logo.
• Browse movies and shows by genre in Search, with separate movie and series results.
• Library hero content and title logos are centered, with matching TMDB artwork available when Fanart.tv has no logo.
• The welcome screen shows official movie and show posters, and its sign-in form is easier to read.
• Library row panels take up less space while keeping the artwork at its original size.
• Fixed removing IPTV providers and media servers from Settings.

apps.name: Lineup tvOS
apps.subtitle: Live television, sports, and your media library on Apple TV
apps.localizedDescription: Lineup brings your IPTV provider and your media servers to Apple TV. Browse live channels in the TV guide, open a game in Sports right on the channel showing it, and watch movies and shows from Jellyfin, Emby, Plex or Silo, picking up where you left off. Request what's missing through Seerr. Inspired by Janky and Stadium-Sync.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Seerr requests go season by season, and you'll see why a title or season can't be requested instead of a generic error.
• Setting up Silo works with the address from its docs page, and playback sessions end properly when you stop watching.
• If the sports schedule can't refresh because of a secure connection problem, it tells you that.

• Immersive lighting stays inside the black bars during playback. The light bands are half as deep.
• Scrolling through Library posters does less work, and moving focus stops animated artwork from decoding after you leave a card.
• Coming back from the screensaver is smoother, especially with a large watch history or a connected Jellyfin server.
• Stream results show the release’s file size when the server provides it, including when you use your server’s formatter.

• Shows you're caught up on stay in Continue Watching, with the next episode's air date, or a Coming Soon card until one is scheduled.
• With two servers connected, like Nullfin and AIOStreams, a movie or show shows up once in Continue Watching, and your progress reaches both servers whichever one played it.
• Continue Watching keeps up with your iPhone: something you finish there moves on here too.
• Nullfin and other Jellyfin servers' streams now show exactly the way your formatter writes them, like AIOStreams' do.
• Games that won't load move to another channel within about 15 seconds instead of minutes, and Lineup remembers channels that failed and tries the working ones first next time.
• Ambient Mode spreads the picture's colours into any black bars around it. Turn it off in Metadata settings.
• Search lists its genres from A to Z, and show names in the guide no longer carry the tiny raised "New" some providers add.

• Your progress now syncs with Jellyfin, Emby and AIOStreams. The server knows where you stopped, and what you watch in other apps shows up in Continue Watching and Next Up.
• Animated covers play on the card you're on and stop when you move away.
• AIOStreams streams are listed exactly the way your formatter writes them, and badge packs you add in Metadata settings put picture badges under each stream.
• AIOStreams streams come up faster: Lineup starts finding them as soon as you open a movie or episode.
• Posters from your own server, such as ones from a poster service, now stay put instead of being swapped for TMDB's.
• Late games that run past midnight stay on Sports until they end, wherever you are.

• Lineup on Apple TV is simpler and much faster. Sports is now a list of game cards like on iPhone: select a game to watch it full screen, or hold select for channels, reminders, team pages and more.
• In the TV Guide, Back takes you to the top of the guide, and Back again to the menu bar. Browsing channels no longer starts a video for each one; select a channel to watch it.
• Library shows all your shelves in one scrolling list.
• Scrolling is smoother on every tab. If the screen ever freezes for a moment, Settings › Screen Stalls shows when and what was happening.
• Finishing the newest episode of a show that's still airing keeps your place instead of jumping to the specials or back to the first episode.
• Episode cards show the air date and running time right under the episode's name, and adding an AIOStreams server sets up your Library straight away.

• The posters in Library's Streaming Services row now come to life. The one you're on shows art from that service's most popular titles you can play, drifting slowly and fading to the next title every few seconds; the rest hold a still picture until you move to them.
• With Reduce Motion on, every poster shows a still picture instead.
• With an AIOStreams server added, Library opens faster and stays lighter: Lineup no longer loads every one of your catalogs each time you open the app.

• Fixed live-event syncing appearing stuck at 99%. Previously prepared live events remain ready to play while channels and guide data refresh in the background.
• Improved remote navigation across Sports, TV Guide, Library and Settings, especially with large channel and media libraries.
• The Sports background now fills the entire screen with the highlighted event's dark team-color blend, including behind the navigation bar and scores ticker.
• Live scores refresh independently of channel matching, and tennis events keep their prepared channels when tournament listings change.
• Added soccer coverage for the Carabao Cup, FA Cup, Copa del Rey and Supercopa de España.

• Settings has a new charcoal layout with a fixed category sidebar and more room for controls. The extra description panel and footer text are gone.
• Sports backgrounds follow the highlighted game's dark team-color blend, with smooth transitions as you browse.
• Channel matching shares background work and avoids unnecessary repeat downloads. Saved games remain available while provider data refreshes.
• Reduced rendering work in Sports and Settings, including during rapid remote navigation.

• Saved live events and their matched channels are ready when you reopen Lineup, while schedules and TV listings refresh in the background.
• Newly available live-game feeds can become playable before the rest of the schedule has finished preparing.
• Once matching finishes for a selected game, Lineup continues automatically instead of repeatedly asking you to wait.
• The data refresh popup now appears only in TV Guide.

• Playlist guides that wouldn't load now do. Lineup used to throw out a whole guide over one badly written listing, a very large guide or a slow guide server, which left the TV Guide empty and Sports with nothing to match.
• A listing Lineup can't read is now skipped on its own, so the rest of the guide still shows.

• The AetherEngine player is updated to 7.49.0, and Settings shows the new version.
• With Match Frame Rate on, films made at exactly 24 frames per second now switch your TV to 24 Hz rather than 23.976 Hz, so they no longer repeat a frame about every 40 seconds.
• Resuming a film or an episode no longer jumps to 0:00 for a moment as it starts, which could also save your place as the very beginning.
• Pressing Play after a pause no longer flashes the loading spinner.
• Some MP4 videos that stuttered or showed frames out of order now play smoothly, and MP4s with lots of subtitle tracks no longer keep stopping to buffer.
• Films with picture-based subtitles, such as those from Blu-rays, use far less memory.
• Includes a security fix for teletext captions on TV channels.

• After Set Up with iPhone, a show now picks up on whichever device was further along, so the TV no longer jumps back to an earlier episode you last played on your iPhone.
• If your iPhone is ahead in a show, the TV moves on to where you are.
• Episodes and movies finished on either device still count as watched, and where both have played the same one, the further point wins.

• New: Set Up with iPhone, at the top of Settings and on the first screen. Scan the code with your iPhone and everything arrives without typing a thing on the remote.
• Your IPTV providers, media servers and their sign-ins come straight across your Wi-Fi, along with MDBList, Seerr, favorites, My Teams and your settings. They load right away, with no restart.
• Watch history from your iPhone joins the TV's own. Nothing either device has watched is lost, and where both played the same title, the most recent play wins.
• A server or provider the TV already has stays one entry instead of showing up twice, and running the setup again tidies up any doubles left from before.

• Text across the app now uses Apple's own rounded system font instead of one bundled with Lineup, so the download is a little smaller.
• From now on, every build has its own number, so your signing app will always offer a new release as an update. That's why this one jumps from 100 to 674.

• Your watch history and favorites take up far less space, so a long history no longer runs into Apple TV's limit on saved settings. Resume points, watched marks and favorites are all kept.
• Subtitles you download while watching no longer pile up after you close the app.
• If the last update didn't show up in your signing app, this one will. It has a new build number.

• Game rows on the Sports tab now read like a scoreboard: each team's crest, name and record at either end, the score in the middle, and the arena and its city underneath.
• Crests, team names, scores and arena details are much larger, so a game is easy to read from across the room.
• Signing in to Silo now works like Jellyfin and Emby, with a choice between your account and an API key.

• Movie and show logos now load independently of the rest of the page, so a slow artwork source does not hold up the others.
• Returning to a title reuses its loaded logo. Matching artwork links are also remembered between app launches.
• Opening a title from Nullfin no longer starts a stream lookup that the details page does not need.
• Added Seerr discovery and requests, plus Silo library connections, with sign-in screens styled for each service.
• Choose local tracking, MDBList, or both. Improved how saved progress and watched status are kept in step.
• Updated menus and supporting screens to match the darker Sports and TV Guide look.
• Apple TV gets the new red play icon, including matching Home Screen and Top Shelf artwork.
